notes.title: Quick guide on how to start
notes.content:
Ahoy, fellow strategists!

I’m David, the solo dev behind VRShogiMates—also known as the guy responsible for making a perfectly good game and then hiding the “Start Game” button behind 3 layers of mystery.

If you’re wondering how to play solo / or with others:

Grab the game piece (e.g. Shogi, Chess, Gungi, etc.)

Open or reopen the menu (left hand)

Click “Host”

Enter any room name (literally anything)

Click “Host” again—boom, you’re in!

Yeah… it’s a bit weird right now. I’m working on making this more intuitive in future updates. In the meantime, thank you so much for your patience, curiosity, and the hilarious reviews—reading them has honestly been the best part of my day.

If you ever want a match (or a quick Shogi/Chu Shogi crash course), join the [url=https://discord.gg/Hn9PWkHVwk]discord[/url]! I also run a physical Shogi club too, so I’m always down to teach or play.

Cheers and see you on the virtual board!
– David L. Banfai
Developer, VRShogiMates

notes.title: Developer Announcement #1
notes.content:
Ahoy, fellow strategists!

I'm the developer behind VRShogiMates, and I must say, out of all the games I've developed, this one is my favorite (and, well, the only one so far).

Good news! VRShogiMates is available on both Steam and the Quest Store. If you've already purchased it here, just leave a review mentioning you'd like a Quest key, and we'll provide one—no need to buy twice.

The controls might take some getting used to, but I've got a handy [url=https://youtu.be/btQkvSP99kk?si=TYjbQmMWuhI9ELpD]YouTube tutorial[/url] to guide you (link also on the store page). For those using VR devices beyond Quest or Index, a quick SteamVR input setup (just a few minutes) will have you playing in no time.
I recommend using SteamLink if possible.

So, grab your headset, choose your game mode, and let's make some moves!

Looking forward to hearing your thoughts and strategies in the reviews!
